verdict.rationale: Helicone's webhooks docs name scoring responses and 'real-time evaluation' (scoring LLM responses for quality, safety, and relevance) as a documented use case, so custom code-based scoring is possible. The scorer code runs in the user's own webhook receiver, though, and nothing shows scores being written back to Helicone or a first-class evaluator or metric framework. missing for 10: native custom scorer/evaluator definitions, a score ingestion or metrics API, scores tied to datasets or experiments, documentation depth beyond a one-line use-case mention, independent or hands-on corroboration.
